Shower enclosures

Quadrant and square enclosures fitted with the tray, the glass and the shower set up together. One of ours is fitted into a loft bathroom, tucked under the slope of the roof. Others are square enclosures finished in white metro tiles or cream wall tiles, set beside the toilet. A quadrant enclosure with sliding glass doors runs against white marble-effect wall panels, and another has a vertical mosaic strip up one wall - the tray goes in level and sealed before the glass and the shower itself go on, so there is nowhere for water to find its way out.

What's included

  • Quadrant and square enclosures

  • Electric or mixer shower connected

Photos from our own jobs

Quadrant or square?

A quadrant enclosure suits a corner and takes up less floor space than a square one; a square enclosure gives a bit more room to stand in a long, narrow bathroom. Either way, the tray sits on a firm, level base before anything else goes in. A hinged door needs clearance to swing open, which is worth checking before choosing between hinged and sliding.

Who fits it

Based in Stafford, with 15 years fitting bathrooms across Staffordshire as a team of four, and public liability insurance up to £1,000,000.
